title: Simulated low-field MRI retains pathology-detection signals with reduced small-lesion sensitivity
summary: First posted in July 2021 and journal-published that December, this study used DenseNet-121 classifiers to compare pathology detection in 3T MRI and simulated 64mT-quality images from glioma, stroke and multiple-sclerosis datasets. Patient-separated tests reported similar slice-level AUCs, including 0.97 versus 0.98 for low-grade glioma, while simulated low-field sensitivity declined for smaller lesions. The transformation had limited paired-image and radiologist checks, but omitted field-dependent tissue contrast and device artifacts; these simulations do not establish diagnostic equivalence or clinical performance of an actual low-field scanner.
ai_technology: DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network for pathology detection

evidence.tested: A non-neural image transformation was fitted using three hydrocephalus patients and checked in three additional patients; three radiologists compared paired real/simulated images from ten MS patients. DenseNet-121 classifiers were trained separately on original/simulated images for low-grade glioma (76 subjects), high-grade glioma (259), stroke (28) and MS (20), using approximately 9:1 patient-separated train/test splits. Reported slice-level AUCs were respectively 0.97/0.98, 0.96/0.95, 0.94/0.94 and 0.90/0.87.
evidence.unknown: The simulation approximates resolution/noise but not all field-strength contrast or device-specific artifacts. Separate disease classifiers perform simple lesion detection, not differential diagnosis or full radiologic assessment. Small test cohorts and degraded detection of small lesions limit generalization; prospective actual-device trials and patient benefit were not established.
evidence.ai_role: DenseNet-121, initialized with ImageNet weights, learns lesion-present versus lesion-absent image classification. Comparing held-out original and simulated datasets probes a specific imaging-performance question; the image transformation itself was conventional rather than learned.

source_review.scope: Original journal full text: transformation and radiologist checks, model architecture, patient-separated training, Results, Discussion limits and publication metadata; original medRxiv v1 metadata/abstract compared. Supplements not assessed.
